summary: Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his B.A. from Arizona State University (~1961–1965) and his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1972), later serving as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1977).

Jim Rheingans works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hamburg and a PhD from Bath Spa University and the University of the West of England, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

Jin Kyoung Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Choi studied as a doctoral student and served as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026), and also held a teaching post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and has been a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jin-il Chung works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Chung has held appointments at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, serving as a Mitarbeiter (attested 2008) and as a Redaktor (attested 2026).

Jinah Kim works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley (attested 2007) under Joanna Gottfried Williams, was a Mellon fellow at IAS (2009–2010), and became Professor at Harvard University (attested 2026).
Jinavijaya Muni was an Indologist and historian who served as Principal at Gujarat Vidyapith and founded the Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959).

Jinbo Shi is a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Minzu University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang, he held appointments at CASS from 1975, Minzu University, and North Minzu University.
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who has held professorships at National Central University (attested 2010) and Fo Guang University (attested 2010).
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995) and served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. ~1963–1967), later serving as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingru Wang was a linguist and historian who studied at Tsinghua University (~1926–1929) and held a post at Minzu University of China from approximately 1952 to 1990.
Jingyi Yang is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies who has studied and served as a research project staff member at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University, he became a professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll and Yunji Chen. Jia has held posts at CU Boulder, Harvard, and Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Jinshi Fan is a historian and archaeologist in Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University (~1958–1963) under Su Bai and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy from 1984 to 2014.

Jinzhang Peng was an archaeologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He was deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and later served as archaeological institute dean and professor at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).
